Subject: Pricing & Context-Length: token volumes and pricing qualification

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alex — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we can align on pricing and sizing: 

What we covered:
- Primary use case: interactive customer support assistant + nightly summarization job.
- Latency target: sub-1.5s for interactive flows (95th) for standard queries.
- Data sensitivity: low/medium for support transcripts; will use Private/Dedicated if we proceed.

Follow-ups I need from you to finish a pricing / packaging proposal (see attached token profile template):
1) Estimated avg prompt tokens and avg completion tokens across the product (or by flow if easier).
2) Monthly token volume (prompts vs completions) or an approximate monthly spend budget.
3) Rough distribution of context-length needs: percent of calls that need >8k, >32k, >128k.
4) Any SLOs or hard requirements that would force higher-cost variants (e.g., 100% 128k availability).

Attachment: acme_token_profile.csv (template) — please fill the short table with sample prompts/completions and the monthly estimate. If you prefer, a quick reply with the numbers in-line works too.

Planned next step: once we get the profile, Connor will validate the context-length implications and we’ll share a blended pricing proposal showing $/1M tokens for the standard 8k profile and uplift tiers for 32k/128k variants.

Best,

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Date: 2026-08-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & Context-Length: token volumes and pricing qualification

Thanks Marissa — attaching our filled profile (acme_token_profile_filled.csv). Quick answers inline below to save time: 

- Avg prompt tokens: 150 tokens (typical customer message + metadata).
- Avg completion tokens: 900 tokens (ranged, some long explanations).
- Monthly token volumes (approx, combined across prod & staging): ~200M tokens / month total (prompts ~30M, completions ~170M).
- Context-length distribution (by request):
  - ~70% under 2k tokens (short chats)
  - ~20% between 2k-8k
  - ~8% between 8k-32k (detailed tickets + extended context)
  - ~1.8% over 32k up to 64k
  - ~0.2% require 128k+ (rare, multi-hour conversation stitching for audit)

Budget guidance: current pilot budget for inference is $10k-15k/month. Ideally we’d like to see unit economics that get us near $50-80 / 1M tokens for the standard workload. For the tail (32k/128k) we expect a material uplift and would accept higher $/1M for those requests.

Let us know if you need more granularity (flow-by-flow). We can set up a short technical call if Connor wants to probe the 32k/128k use cases.

Cheers,
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Platform | Acme Corp

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & Context-Length: token volumes and pricing qualification

Quick analysis based on Alex's numbers (200M tokens/month, prompt 150 / completion 900 avg, tail 8% 8k-32k, ~2% >32k, 0.2% 128k):

1) Unit economics (target buckets)
   - If Acme's target is $10k/month on 200M tokens -> effective $/1M = $10k / 200 = $50 per 1M tokens. That actually hits the low end of their $50-80 target.

2) Context-length impact and recommended pricing approach
   - Standard (<=8k): this will cover ~98% of latency-sensitive traffic. Recommend base $/1M = $60 (includes standard 8k caches/batching).
   - 32k-class requests (8%): route to a 32k-optimized variant with a 2.5x uplift => $150 / 1M equivalent tokens. Use request-based routing to apply uplift only to those requests.
   - 128k-class (0.2%): route to a high-memory node with larger KV handling and slower throughput; recommend a 10x uplift => $600 / 1M equivalent. Offer a blended estimate and a fall-through policy to avoid unexpected spend.

3) Cost reduction opportunities to hit their $50-80 target
   - Prefix/KV caching on repeated conversational context (could cut completion tokens by ~20-30% for support flows).
   - Serve summarized context for archival-heavy flows (pre-summarize long histories into a shorter vector).
   - Offer a commit/discount structure: $60/1M with 6–12 month commit gets them closer to $40/1M effective.

4) Next steps for proposal
   - Draft a blended pricing quote that models their 200M tokens/month and applies the 32k/128k uplifts only to the tail. I attached a sketch of the draft pricing quote.
   - Schedule a 30m technical deep-dive to validate 32k/128k examples and confirm latency SLO trade-offs (Connor + Rishi + Acme infra).

Attachment: pricing_quote_draft.pdf (pdf, 95KB)

I can spin an explicit per-flow cost model if they share a short sample of 1k requests (we can run a quick profiler to estimate batching benefits).

-Connor
